extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level tasks. It contains 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected/created by over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant majors, who served as annotators. They gathered multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, created new questions when needed, followed copyright/licensing rules, and were advised to avoid questions with immediately available answers. Quality control included duplicate detection with author review, format/typo checking by co-authors, and author-assigned difficulty categorization, with very easy items removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control and annotation/error analysis were performed through duplicate detection and review, format/typo checking, difficulty categorization, and later expert analysis of 150 GPT-4V error cases; the paper also notes 2% annotation error among analyzed errors.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One annotator collected/created each question, with subsequent review/QC by authors/co-authors; no multiple independent labels per item are reported.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university/college students, including co-authors, specializing in various disciplines/majors corresponding to the benchmark subjects.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may contain biases from its manual curation process, and model analysis notes a bias toward textual information over visual inputs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited by possible curation bias, incomplete coverage for testing Expert AGI, and uneven generalization across image types and difficult expert-level tasks. It is not a sufficient standalone test for Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is framed as socially important for monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled human labor, creating risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating multimodal models' college-level, expert-oriented perception, knowledge, and reasoning. It provides a few-shot development set, a validation set for hyperparameter selection, and a test set; experiments are conducted in zero-shot settings, with some few-shot results also reported.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to remove duplicates, format and typo checking with standardized formatting corrections, and exclusion of about 10% very easy problems that did not meet design criteria.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary... The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations... the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers... lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning... lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... reviewed by the authors... format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels” and “We meticulously examine 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V’s predictions... The remaining errors include... Annotation Error (2%)”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “we recruit over 50 university students... as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions...” and “These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking.”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects” and “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: "MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases"; "Additionally, GPT-4V often exhibits a bias towards text, prioritizing textual information over visual inputs"

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI"; "We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI"; "This indicates that the existing models are generalizing poorly towards these image types."

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: "Expert AGI... starting to achieve 'the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor' for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI."

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models"; "The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions."; "Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting"

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... ensure adherence to a standardized format... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy... are excluded from the benchmark.”
